newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya opposition party urges boycott to topple Moi.
newsitem.headline: Kenya opposition party urges boycott to topple Moi.

text.p: Kenya's opposition FORD-Asili party called on Wednesday for a mass action programme including a boycott of businesses to topple President Daniel arap Moi.
FORD-Asili Chairman Kenneth Matiba told a news conference his party was calling for a constitutional conference among the widest possible spectrum of Kenyans to decide on reforms.
His statement was one of the first signs of rifts among an opposition-backed alliance which united Moi's usually divided enemies to campaign for political reforms before the polls.
"FORD-Asili demands that Moi step aside so as not to interfere with the process of constitutional reform," he said.

"On their part, Kenyans must begin a mass action programme including the boycott of shops and businesses that support Moi's dictatorship," added Matiba, who failed to register for this year's general election and cannot stand for the presidency.
"We are determined to remove Moi from State House if he does not go voluntarily. We shall ensure that he is not harmed so that he can see you can rule people without killing them.
"We also want his huge sums of money salted out of the country repatriated, not because we want to grab it but so that it may be used to develop this country," Mabita added.

Other opposition parties have united behind the National Convention Executive Council (NCEC), an alliance of parties, civil groups and other bodies demanding political reforms that will reduce the power of Moi, 73 and president for 19 years.
Moi has attempted this month to pull the reform rug out from under the NCEC's feet by agreeing to some political reforms before this year's elections and a review of the constitution.

Moi's government blunted an opposition-backed rally in the Indian Ocean city of Mombasa at the weekend by licensing it after clashes elsewhere in June and July between police and reform demonstrators rattled foreign investors and tourists.
